passages.title: A – Murder at Kingsbridge Station
passages.text: Set in 1920s Manchester, this detective novel follows Inspector Ruth Hale as she tries to find out who killed a railway worker on a foggy winter night. Readers love the careful details of life a hundred years ago. As well as the paperback, there is an excellent audiobook version, read by the actor Tom Reeves, which lasts eleven hours.

passages.title: B – Two Wheels, One World
passages.text: In this true story, journalist Mark Olsen describes the three years he spent cycling around the world, from the deserts of Australia to the mountains of Peru. At over 600 pages, it is a long read, but it is full of amazing photos. It is only available as a large hardback, which would look lovely on a coffee table.

passages.title: C – Cheap and Cheerful Cooking
passages.text: Written for students and anyone cooking for themselves for the first time, this book has sixty easy recipes that each cost less than three pounds a portion. Every recipe has a series of photos showing each step, from chopping onions to serving the finished dish. There's also a useful chapter on what to keep in your cupboard.

passages.title: D – From Garden to Table
passages.text: Top chef Anna Price shares the secrets of her country kitchen. The first half explains how to grow twenty kinds of vegetables in a large garden and is aimed at people with some experience. The second half has impressive recipes for dinner parties, many needing special equipment and ingredients from expensive food shops. The pictures are beautiful drawings rather than photos.

passages.title: E – Small Space, Big Harvest
passages.text: You don't need a garden to grow your own food. This practical guide shows how to grow tomatoes, lettuce, beans and herbs in pots on a balcony or windowsill. It assumes you know nothing about plants, so it starts with the basics, like choosing soil and watering. Each short chapter ends with a simple checklist.

passages.title: F – Walking Home
passages.text: When Jess Carter lost her job, she decided to walk from London back to her family's farm in Wales. This short, true account of her twelve-day journey is only 150 pages long and is perfect for reading in small pieces. It is published as an e-book, so you can download it straight to your phone or tablet.

passages.title: G – The Cat Who Solved Crimes
passages.text: Victorian London is the setting for this very funny detective story, told by Whiskers, a clever cat who helps his owner catch thieves. Readers of all ages will laugh out loud. Sadly, the author has said that this will be the only book about Whiskers. It is available in paperback, but there is no audio version.

passages.title: H – Max Moves In
passages.text: Fourteen-year-old Max has to share a bedroom with his annoying cousin, and the result is one disaster after another. Teenage readers say it's the funniest book they've read this year. The good news is that it's the first in a series: the next two books about Max and his cousin are already in the shops, and a fourth is coming soon.

questions.question: Maria wants to read a true story about a journey. She reads on her phone on the train to work and would like something she can finish in a week or two.
options: G) The Cat Who Solved Crimes
questions.explanation: Walking Home is a 'true account' of a twelve-day walk, is 'only 150 pages long' and is 'an e-book, so you can download it straight to your phone'. Two Wheels, One World is also a true story about a journey, but it is 'over 600 pages' and 'only available as a large hardback', so Maria cannot read it on her phone.

questions.question: Tom has just moved into his first flat and doesn't have much money for food. He wants to learn to make simple meals and likes to see pictures of how to do every stage.
options: G) The Cat Who Solved Crimes
questions.explanation: Cheap and Cheerful Cooking is for people 'cooking for themselves for the first time', has 'easy recipes' costing 'less than three pounds a portion' and 'photos showing each step'. From Garden to Table also has recipes, but they are 'impressive recipes for dinner parties' with ingredients 'from expensive food shops', and it has drawings, not step-by-step photos.

questions.question: Hannah is fourteen and loves books that make her laugh. When she enjoys a book, she always wants to go on reading about the same characters in other books.
options: G) The Cat Who Solved Crimes
questions.explanation: Max Moves In is 'the funniest book' teenage readers have read this year, and 'it's the first in a series', with more books 'about Max and his cousin'. The Cat Who Solved Crimes is also 'very funny', but 'this will be the only book about Whiskers', so Hannah could not read more about the same characters.

questions.question: David drives a long way to work every day and would like to listen to a detective story in the car. He is especially interested in stories about the past.
options: G) The Cat Who Solved Crimes
questions.explanation: Murder at Kingsbridge Station is a 'detective novel' set in '1920s Manchester', with 'details of life a hundred years ago', and there is 'an excellent audiobook version' David can listen to while driving. The Cat Who Solved Crimes is also a detective story set in the past (Victorian London), but 'there is no audio version'.

questions.question: Lucy lives in a flat with a small balcony and wants to grow her own vegetables. She has never done any gardening before.
options: G) The Cat Who Solved Crimes
questions.explanation: Small Space, Big Harvest shows how to grow vegetables 'in pots on a balcony or windowsill' and 'assumes you know nothing about plants'. From Garden to Table also explains how to grow vegetables, but 'in a large garden', and it is 'aimed at people with some experience', so it is wrong for Lucy.
